name: Florida

regulator.name: Florida Department of Business and Professional Regulation (DBPR)

law.name: Florida athlete agent licensing (Fla. Stat. 468.45 and following)

covers_nil_agents: Yes. A license is required for NIL representation of college athletes (Fla. Stat. 468.453(8)).
summary: Get a license from DBPR. $630 plus fingerprints. Renews May 31 of even years.

steps.detail: Application for Licensure as an Athlete Agent. You must be 18+.
Electronic fingerprints for the state and FBI background check. The cost depends on the vendor.
Online at myfloridalicense.com, or mail to: DBPR Central Intake Unit, 2601 Blair Stone Road, Tallahassee, FL 32399-0783.

steps.text: Optional: ask for a temporary license
steps.detail: Written request with your name, address and SSN. It is good for 60 days and can't be extended.

steps.text: Tell the athletic director before you first contact the athlete about NIL
Use a written contract with all required items
steps.detail: Your pay and how it's calculated, anyone else being paid, expenses, services, length and date signed.

steps.text: Put the WARNING TO STUDENT ATHLETE box next to their signature
Use separate contracts for NIL and for pro or athletic representation
Give the athlete a copy when they sign
Notify the athletic director within 72 hours of signing
steps.detail: Or before the athlete's next game, whichever comes first. The athlete may cancel within 14 days.
Names and addresses, contracts and recruiting costs.

steps.text: Report a new address or name with Form DBPR AA-4102
Never give gifts or money to recruit athletes, or pay coaches or school staff for referrals

steps.detail: Every even year. The next renewal is May 31, 2028. The state emails you 90 to 120 days before. No classes are required.

watch_list.item: Federal Protect College Sports Act of 2026 (S.4668)
watch_list.status: Passed the Senate on Sept 28, 2026. The House is out until Nov 9 and leaders say it won't pass as-is. It dies if not enacted by Jan 3, 2027.
watch_list.impact: It would require every NIL agent to register in a state, cap agent fees at 5% of an endorsement deal and limit contracts to the athlete's eligibility.

review_notes: The contract, records and licensing statute text was pulled from the 2017 edition of the Florida Statutes. The 2026 text should be checked for changes.
Penalties exist (acting unlicensed and missing the athletic director notice have historically been felonies), but the current penalty sections were not reviewed yet.
